She got to the soft drink factory at 9 instead of 8.30. Her new boss, who is a tall and fat man, was very angry. He taught her what to do in a rush. In 1834, the government tried to solve the problem in another way. It declared that all the land west of the Mississippi River would be a permanent home for the Native Americans. The Native American people from the East protested, but they were forced to move. Subsequently, many of them died on the long journey W. It wasn't long, however, until this promise was broken as well. In 1848, gold was discovered in California. Thousands of Americans moved W again the Indians protested, but the government did nothing.

d120.text: 120. By 1890 the fighting between the Native Americans and the government had ended. The tribes that were left were forced to live on reservations, small areas of land that the government had given them. Life on the reservations was not pleasant. The reservations were placed under the control of a government agency, the Bureau of Indian Affairs. The people who worked for the agency understood little about the Indians. They wanted them to give up their languages and traditions and accept a different way of life. The Native Americans, however, refused to give up their cultural identity. Today there are about 800,000 Native Americans living in the United States. Over half of them live on reservations. There are about 300 reservations located throughout 28 states. Many Native Americans are working to improve conditions on the reservations. They are proud of their traditions, history, and languages.

d121.text: 121. Many scientists and economists believe that food production will not keep up with population growth. No one knows how many people the Earth can support, but many people believe that the world will soon be overpopulated. There will be more people than the Earth can support. For many years, the world population increased slowly. Because of poor health care, death rates were very high. Then during the 18th century, living conditions began to improve and people learned to control many diseases. As a result, the death rate began to drop and the population grew quickly. Certainly if the population continues to grow at its present rate, the world population will double in 35 years. Many people believe that such a high population would cause famines, wars and other disasters.

d123.text: 123. Our present supply of fresh water is controlled by the process of evaporation and distillation of the oceans by the sun's energy. Water evaporates from the surface of the ocean, but the amount of water in the air must remain about the same. As a result, the water that evaporates falls back in the form of precipitation, rain and snow. The sources of fresh water on the continents lose 70,000 cubic kilometers of water each year through the process of evaporation. They receive 110,000 cubic kilometers of precipitation each year. The result is that 40,000 cubic kilometers of fresh water are transferred from the oceans to the continents each year.

d126.text: 126. The oceans cover more than 70% of the Earth's surface. The Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Arctic, and Antarctic oceans are really one large body of water broken by the islands that we call continents. The fishing industry, however, produces only a small percentage of the world's food. Oceanographers are seeking ways to increase the amount of food taken from the ocean. Many undersea plants contain vitamins and minerals. Perhaps in the future people will be able to grow these plants on undersea farms.

The ocean cannot hold too much of these things without endangering its fish and plants. As the world population increases, people will need more products from the sea. d166.text: 166. No author in American literature is better known or more loved than Samuel Langorn Clemens. Why should they go to a strange land far beyond the Mississippi River? The army was sent to drive the Cherokee out. Soldiers surrounded their villages and marched them at gunpoint into the western territory. More than 4,000 Cherokee died during the terrible march. They called that march the Trail of Tears. The end of the trail was also the end of the Great Cherokee Nation.

d190.text: 190. It's been quite some time since I was last in London, but something happened during that visit that I'll remember as long as I live. London had one of the thickest fogs in years. You could hardly see your hand in front of your face. Cars and buses crept along, their lights on and their horn blowing furiously. When evening fell, the weather got even worse. The fog was as thick as pea soup. All traffic came to a standstill. I had an important meeting on the other side of town, but it was impossible to find a taxi. I decided to walk and started out confidently. Minutes later I was completely lost. I couldn't even find a street sign to get my bearings.

d191.text: 191. Then I heard a voice come out of the fog. I suppose you are lost. Can I help you? I could barely see the young woman who had spoken to me but was grateful to find another person out in the fog. I explained where I wanted to go and she said she knew exactly how to get there. I was doubtful but followed her through the dark streets. The city seemed as quiet as a graveyard and I remember thinking my guide could be leading me to an alley where she and some friends would rob me. But my fears were unfounded. The woman led me straight to my destination. I was amazed at how well she had found her way through the fog. I know this part of town quite well, she replied. But the fog, this terrible fog, made it impossible to see anything, I said. But what do you suppose she answered?

d192.text: 192. The original inhabitants of Australia are called Aborigines. Most of them live in the desert areas of Australia. These people do not plant crops and they don't keep any domesticated animals. They wander through the deserts in search of food and water. They must depend on their ability to track down wild animals to stay alive. It's not an easy life. It has been said that an Aborigine has the eyes of an eagle and the heart of a lion. The Aborigine's astonishing skill at tracking is illustrated by this story. A gold robbery in a small Australian town had left the police puzzled. They called an old Aborigine tracker for help. The tracker found a set of boot prints in the dusty St. and said he thought they were the tracks of the thief.

d193.text: 193. Before the tracker could follow the prints very far, however, a flash rainstorm broke and washed the tracks away. Sometime after that, the aborigine was in another town, and his sharp eyes picked out the same boot prints he had seen days before. The police could hardly believe his story, but they accompanied him as he followed the trail through the dirt streets and past the outskirts of town. The tracker stopped near an old abandoned cabin and simply pointed. And sure enough, the wanted man was hiding inside. Fewer and fewer Aborigines live the traditional desert life now. But no matter where they settle or what new ways of life they try, they still have the amazing hunting skills of their ancestors.

d194.text: 194. One of the biggest events in a child's life is the coming of the circus to town. Early in the morning the circus train pulls into town and immediately preparations begin for hoisting the big top. Tons of canvas are unrolled, men shout and strain, the circus elephants help hoist the huge tent poles into place. Soon what had previously been a vacant lot becomes a miniature canvas city. This city is populated by a host of strange personalities. Lion tamers, acrobats, freaks, all are citizens of the greatest show on earth.

A moment of carelessness and the lion tamer may be mauled and crippled by one of his huge cats. These men are used to danger and take it as a matter of course. Most of them come from circus families. They have been trained from childhood to become performers under the big top. Their art, like the art of the ancient craft guilds, is handed down from generation to generation.

d196.text: All circus performers are not men of skill and daring. The freaks are a group of entertainers who are interesting or unusual simply because of some physical deformity or strange talent. Every circus has a fat lady, a tall man, a snake charmer, a sword swallower, and many others. These people are all pathetic in a way, but perhaps the fat lady is most to be pitied. She doesn't mind the stares of the crowd so much, but the summer heat is almost unbearable. What's more, she knows that if she goes on a diet to relieve her misery, she will probably lose her job.

d197.text: 197. One indispensable member of the circus troupe is the clown. His antics and stunts delight children of all ages. Even grown-ups are not immune to the humorous appeal of the clown. His carefree jokes and pranks provide a pleasant escape from the routine of everyday life. Yet surprisingly enough, one of the most beloved clowns of the modern circus world is a sad-faced hobo. In real life, this clown is Emmett Kelly, the foremost circus clown of our day. His winsome humor and pathetic loneliness have captivated the hearts of circus audiences the world over. Almost always, the clown is the most popular member of the circus troupe.

d198.text: 198. It is often pointed out that cats possess a great curiosity. A cat will poke his nose into every nook and cranny of the house in an attempt to satisfy his curiosity. Sometimes his curiosity gets him into trouble. One cat poked his head into a hole in the ground to find out what was in it. He never forgot. A skunk was living in the hole and liberally sprayed the poor cat with his vile smelling perfume. It took about a month for the odor to wear away. During that time, the cat was not allowed near the house. He had become a real social outcast because of his curiosity.

d199.text: 199. Curiosity can get men into trouble too. The classic story of misfortune brought about by excessive curiosity is contained in the Old Testament. When God destroyed the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, he warned one man to flee with his family. He cautioned this man Lot that he and his family must not look back during their flight. Lot obeyed this command and escaped safely, but his wife gave in to her curiosity and glanced back to see what was happening in the cities. No sooner had she looked than she was turned into a pillar of salt. Nowadays, a woman who is excessively curious may often be returned to as a modern Lot's wife.

His curiosity led him to discover electricity and to invent many things that have contributed to the comfort of our daily life. The curiosity of a Dutch scientist prompted him to investigate the world of a drop of water through a set of lenses. This was the forerunner of the modern microscope and has enabled great advancement to be made in the science of medicine.

d201.text: There is a famous short story which whets the reader's curiosity, only to leave him in bewilderment at the end. This story, The Lady or the Tiger, is about a curious form of punishment. Instead of criminals being punished with death or imprisonment, they would be placed in a small room containing 2 doors. Behind one door was a beautiful lady. Behind the other was a savage tiger. If the victim made the right choice, he would escape unharmed. The author, however, ends his story just as the young man opens one of the doors. We never know which came out, the lady or the tiger.

d202.text: 202. No one will dispute the fact that kindness is a fine virtue. To say a person is kind is to say that he is gentle, considerate, and charitable. He puts the comfort of others before his own convenience. In looking back over the people we have known and loved, we can all remember certain men and women who were outstanding for their kindness. Perhaps the teacher who lives most vividly in our memory is the one who was kind and gentle. He may not have been outstandingly brilliant, but nevertheless he probably taught us a lesson in kindness, more important than mere academic learning. Kindness is a gentle virtue. It not only brightens our own lives, but also fills the lives of our friends and associates with happiness.

d203.text: 203. In talking about virtues, however, we must take an old Roman proverb into consideration. Virtue takes the middle course. If virtue becomes excessive, it can easily turn into a vice. For example, excessive humility might easily become hypocrisy or cowardice. Excessive love for our friends or children might be considered to be a manifestation of selfishness. But it is difficult to say that excessive kindness become a vice. Rather, excessive kindness is usually motivated by entirely good intentions. It merely fails to take the wants and desires of others into consideration.

d204.text: 204. There was once a kindly old lady who ran a boarding house in San Francisco. She really had the best interests of her lodgers at heart. Whenever she acquired a new roomer, she always took in one of her freshly baked peach pies. For years she had delighted in watching the smile of appreciation that her thankful boarders turned upon her for the simple act of kindness. One day, however, when she took one of her steaming pies to a new border, he politely refused the delicacy. The woman was a little hurt, but insisted that the man eat a piece then and there. He made many attempts to refuse, saying that pastry did not agree with him. But the woman would not take no for an answer, and finally the poor man gave in and ate a piece of pie. That night he died of indigestion.

In fact, sometimes our good intentions can put others to serious inconvenience. An old saying puts it this way, one man's meat is another man's poison.

d206.text: 206. American students are notorious for playing practical jokes. Several years ago, the statue of the founder of a certain university disappeared from its place of honor in the center of the campus. Naturally, the school authorities were quite upset and began a search for the missing statue. Finally, it was found standing in a rowboat which had been left floating in the middle of one of the campus lakes. The statue was holding a fishing pole and during the night a fish had taken the bait and had been captured. The school authorities were furious but some people say that the statue seemed to be smiling. The founder had enjoyed fishing during his life and the student prank had enabled him to indulge in his favorite sport once more.

d210.text: 210. Throughout recorded history, we find that one of the most interesting forms of collections has been that of living animals. Ancient Rome and Alexandria were noted for their huge zoos where animals from all over the then known world were gathered together and placed on exhibition. Today, large cities the world over have modern zoos designed to acquaint people with the animals of their own and of foreign countries. But in addition to being instructive, the zoo is one of the favorite spots of Sunday afternoon pleasure seekers. In viewing the strange animals, birds, and reptiles, the visitor to a zoo gets a taste of far-off exotic lands. For those who cannot afford to travel, going to a zoo is almost like taking a trip to a foreign country.

d214.text: 214. Man is afraid of the unknown. In an attempt to explain the unknown, primitive man fashioned various kinds of superstitions. The sound of thunder, for example, was thought to be the roar of battle and war between fearful gods in the heavens. Lightning was supposedly the sparks from their weapons, and rain was thought to be the tears of the gods. In his ignorance, primitive man thought that the capricious gods used natural calamities such as storms, earthquakes, and hurricanes to take their spite out on the dwellers of the earth. Accordingly, priests played an important role in primitive societies by praying to the angry gods and begging them to refrain from plaguing man with such calamities.

d215.text: 215 In addition to the intercession of the priests, primitive man had many good luck charms designed to protect him from evil. These charms also served the purpose of giving him bravery when confronted with danger or when engaged in battle. Many of the American Indians, for example, made a practice of hanging the scalps of their conquered foes on a belt which they wore around their waists. These scalps were considered to be good luck charms which made their wearers immune to physical danger. Many animals were also regarded by the Indians as symbols of good fortune. Some animals, such as the white buffalo, were even worshipped because they were thought to be scared. It is probably true to say that in ancient civilizations superstition took the place of religion.

d245.text: 245. Halloween stems from the Christian feast of All Saints. Literally, Halloween means Holy Eve and refers to the night before All Saints' Day. According to an old superstition, the spirits of the dead supposedly came forth from their graves on the eve of All Saints. In order to light the way for the spirits, the farmers and peasants of Europe lit huge bonfires. Gradually, this custom turned into an all-night celebration during which everyone dressed in weird costumes. This ancient celebration has now turned into the modern holiday of Halloween.

d246.text: 246. Sometimes the rules of etiquette seem to be bothersome, but they are designed to make social relations pleasant. Etiquette is merely acting like a well-bred human being should act. d249.text: 249. People like to be frightened. Not in real life, of course, but through books, movies, and other forms of fiction. There's something very pleasant in a chilling sort of way about reading a good murder mystery or detective story. But even the bravest of men prefer to have someone else in the room with them when they are reading a story designed to make their hair stand on end. When reading a mystery story alone at night, one's imagination is more active than ever. The slightest noise sounds like stealthy footsteps and the voice of the wind becomes more dismal than ever. d251.text: 251. In applying for a job, one should always keep in mind the old truth. First impressions are lasting. Your prospective employer is going to judge you by your appearance, your bearing, and above all by your speech. Before hiring someone for a position, an employer naturally wants to have an interview. The interview gives him a chance to size up the applicant. Most large companies have trained specialists called personnel managers whose job it is to interview and pass judgment on prospective employees. d255.text: 255. Medicine is one of the oldest sciences known to man. Ancient medicine was a combination of magical prayers, charms, and formulas. Powdered goat foot and dried frog eyes seem strange and absurd remedies to modern man, but the ancients took them seriously. They also believed that many illnesses were the result of having displeased the gods. Therefore, the best cure was a prayer or sacrifice that would restore them to the favor of the gods. For this reason, the profession of physician or doctor was usually reserved to the priest caste. This custom persists even today in some of the primitive tribes of Africa and among the American Indians.

In a similar way, the modern age finds expression in the rhythms of jazz and swing.
Even the music of the so-called modern classical composers is characterized by strange rhythms and discords.
A 100 years from now, people will listen to our music and get a taste of the restlessness and vigor of the present age.

d272.text: 272. A few years ago most intellectuals scorned popular music. They thought it had little or no value. But today people are becoming increasingly aware that jazz, swing, and the other forms of 20th century music are a valid and worthwhile trend in music. Today many colleges and universities hold classes in the history of jazz as part of American culture. But there are still some people who refuse to admit the value of jazz. Every family has a maiden aunt who looks down her nose at the young generation's interest in that barbaric racket, but she will listen with pleasure to some of the classical racket of men like Wagner.

d273.text: 273. The story of the Tower of Babel appears in the Old Testament. In an attempt to understand the mysteries of God, man tried to build a tower that would reach to heaven. As a punishment for their pride, the tower collapsed and the language of the workers became confused. This is an allegorical explanation of the origin of the various languages that are spoken throughout the world. Today, more than 1,000 languages are spoken. Many of them stem from a common source. The Romance languages such as French, Spanish, and Italian are all derived from Latin. English, on the other hand, has borrowed elements from many languages. Its vocabulary comes in part from Latin while its grammar is similar to that of German.

d274.text: 274. In the Middle Ages, Latin was the universal language. Most university classes were conducted in Latin and all important documents were written in that language. Gradually, however, Latin fell into disuse and by the 18th century, French had become the language of diplomacy. Today, however, English is commonly used to transact international affairs. For this reason, English is referred to as a universal language. It is becoming increasingly important as a means of overcoming the language barriers that exist between the various countries of the world. It can truly be said that the man who speaks English possesses an important tool for communicating with other people throughout the world.

d275.text: There are various reasons why English has come to occupy the important position it does today. The few dialects in English give it the advantage of being a standard language. In addition, English is very exact. It has few of the ambiguities that are found in many other modern tongues. This makes it ideal for the transaction of business and international affairs. The biggest drawback to English as a universal language, however, is its difficult pronunciation. In addition, the many exceptions to the rules of English usage make it difficult to master. However, the satisfaction of being able to speak this widely used language makes the study of English well worthwhile.

d276.text: 276. Language is one of man's most precious possessions. Without it, he would be unable to exchange ideas with his fellow men. In the modern world, however, it is not enough to speak only the language of one's own country. It is said that the man who speaks 2 languages has two minds, for in learning a foreign language we acquire, to a certain extent, the mentality of a foreign people. Language study accordingly is one of the best means of enabling us to understand our fellow men. It is difficult, to be sure, but rich in rewards. It makes us better citizens of the international world in which we live.
